text:
Sam: Quick thread: follow-up on shrinkback behavior when pool can't honor burst admits. Observed p99 regressions in canary.
Priya: Noted. Can you paste the logs/snippet?
Sam: logs: `admit=fastpath tenant=A cost=3 -> shrinkback triggered; fallthrough to full_reserve delayed 1200ms`
Liang: 1200ms sounds like our backoff on CAS retries. We need bounded fast-path fallback to avoid long stalls.
Nora: Two problems: (1) operator CAS hot loops during restarts, (2) admission path waits for allocator snapshot.
Sam: Proposal: add a hard timeout on fastpath CAS of 100ms, then immediate synchronous handoff to full_reserve.
Priya: Agree. Also add metric `admit.shrinkback.latency` and counter `admit.shrinkback.count` to track frequency.
Liang: For correctness, we should make shrinkback idempotent: multiple callers hitting CAS fail should see the same tenant_soft_burst state. Use redis LUA to apply subtract+ttl atomically.
Nora: LUA is fine but watch redis CPU. Maybe batch updates for high QPS tenants?
Sam: Could we instead do probabilistic decrement and reconcile later? e.g., best-effort decrement and periodic ledger check.
Priya: Risk there is over-admit. We must guarantee no more than tenant_hard_limit tokens admitted concurrently. Probabilistic approach complicates invariants.
Liang: Alternative: use a per-tenant semaphore in the operator (in-memory) plus persistent counter as backup. Operators are sharded by tenant group so it can work. On operator failover, fallback to persistent check.
Nora: Sharded semaphores make sense but increases operator ownership complexity. We'll need leader election per shard. Ops will hate it.
Sam: Another angle: shrinkback should prefer immediate lightweight preemption of queued non-interactive jobs in the same pool to free capacity. That keeps latency low for interactive admits.
Priya: Preemptions need policy: don't preempt another tenant's guaranteed capacity. Only preempt best-effort background workloads. Add label `preemptible=true` to those jobs.
Liang: Implementation sketch for handoff path (pseudo):
```
start_time = now()
if redis.CAS(soft_key, expected, expected-cost, timeout=100ms):
  admit fastpath
else:
  emit(metric: cas_fail)
  call full_reserve_flow(sync=true)
```
Nora: And add a fallback admission mode `shrinkback_fast_failover` that emits sampling traces to compare latency profiles.
Sam: For the canary rollback, we saw certain tenants with burst skewing the global pool. Need per-tenant daily budget + rolling 1h window.
Priya: Add `burst_budget_daily` and `burst_budget_hourly`. When hourly > 50% of daily, start tighter caps.
Liang: Telemetry: surface `burst_utilization` per tenant + pool. Use 1m and 5m rolling windows.
Nora: Ops-bot suggestion: create checklist `shrinkback-mitigation-6543211111` with items: redis-lua-bench, operator-semaphore-proto, metrics-dash, preemptible-labeling.
deploy-bot: created checklist/shrinkback-mitigation-6543211111; created epic/shrinkback-654321.
Sam: Owners? I'll do redis lua prototype (ETA 4d).
Priya: I'll own metrics + rollout gating (ETA 2d).
Liang: I'll spike operator semaphore design and simulate failure modes (ETA 1w).
Nora: I'll coordinate preemptible-job labeling with batch infra (ETA 3d).
Sam: Also callout in RFC: risk of oscillation if shrinkback triggers cascade of preempts -> reclaim -> shrinkback loop. Need dampening factor and circuit breaker.
Priya: Add `shrinkback_cooldown` per pool default 30s and a max_preemptions_per_min to avoid storms.
Liang: Good. Also add sampling traces on transition paths to debug.
Nora: Ok team, sync next Tue 11am with prototype metrics. Short-term rollback plan: feature-flag disable fastpath admit.
Sam: Thanks. I'll post the prototype PR and attach sim results when ready.
